entries.title: Break-even is a contribution statement, not a profit statement
entries.body: BEP (units) = Fixed cost / Contribution per unit. The insight is that break-even is reached when total contribution equals fixed cost — profit is irrelevant at that point. This is why the formula works under any cost structure and why a change in fixed cost moves the BEP one-for-one.

entries.title: Rank by contribution per limiting factor, never per unit
entries.body: When a resource is scarce, the objective is to maximise contribution per unit of the scarce resource. A product with the highest contribution per unit can be the worst choice if it consumes far more of the constraint. This is the single most reliable way to lose marks in Paper 12 and the easiest to get right.

entries.title: I keep including allocated fixed costs in make-or-buy
entries.body: Cause: full-cost habit from product costing. Rule: a cost is relevant only if it is future, incremental and differs between alternatives. Allocated fixed overhead usually continues either way and must be excluded. Opportunity cost of released capacity must be included instead.

entries.title: Sec 139(2) — auditor rotation
entries.body: Listed companies and prescribed classes must rotate their auditor: an individual auditor for one term of five years, an audit firm for two terms of five years, with a five-year cooling-off period. Transitional provisions apply to appointments made before the rule commenced. Cite the section and the class of company, then the consequence.

entries.title: Charge registration — failure makes the security void
entries.body: A charge must be registered with the Registrar within 30 days of creation under section 77. If it is not, the charge is void against the liquidator and creditors under section 85, so the lender ranks as unsecured. The certificate of registration is conclusive evidence that the requirements have been complied with.

entries.title: Income-tax Act, 2025 has replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026
entries.body: The Income-tax Act, 2025 (Act 30 of 2025) received assent on 21 August 2025 and applies to tax year 2026-27 onwards. Tax years up to FY 2025-26 remain governed by the 1961 Act, including pending assessments and appeals. Section numbers change substantially — for example 80C becomes 123, 115BAC becomes 202, and TDS moves into section 393. Confirm which statute is examinable for your attempt from the ICMAI study material edition.
entries.source: Income-tax Act, 2025; verify against ICMAI notification

entries.title: Capital gains indexation withdrawn for most assets from 23 July 2024
entries.body: For transfers on or after 23 July 2024, the long-term capital gains rate is 12.5% without indexation for most assets, with a transitional option for land and buildings acquired before that date where the taxpayer may choose the lower of the two regimes. The exemption limit for listed equity LTCG was also revised. Never quote a rate without stating the transfer date, because the date determines the regime.
entries.source: Finance Act amendments — verify the date and rate for your attempt

entries.title: Why a profitable company runs out of cash
entries.body: Four mechanisms: profit is an accrual measure while cash is a fact, so growth consumes working capital; capital expenditure is cash but is not an expense in the year; loan repayments are cash but not an expense; and revenue recognition can precede collectability. The diagnostic is to reconcile profit to operating cash flow and look at where the gap sits.

entries.title: Absorption versus marginal profit — one reconciliation rule
entries.body: The difference is entirely the fixed production overhead held in stock. If stock rises, absorption profit exceeds marginal profit by the fixed overhead in the increase. If stock falls, absorption profit is lower. If production equals sales, the profits are identical. Memorise the rule, not the direction of each case, and the answer is always right.

entries.title: Contribution is not profit
entries.body: Contribution = sales minus variable cost; it exists to cover fixed cost. Profit = contribution minus fixed cost. In conversation, use 'contribution' when discussing product-level economics and 'profit' only when fixed costs are covered. Conflating them causes pricing errors in practice and lost marks in exams.

entries.title: I stated 'obiter dicta is binding' — wrong
entries.body: Only the ratio decidendi binds lower courts under stare decisis. Obiter dicta are persuasive observations, not binding precedent. The correction is a one-line rule: separate the legal principle necessary to the decision from everything else the judge said.

entries.title: GST credit is a chain, not an entitlement
entries.body: Input tax credit depends on the supplier having actually paid the tax and reported it. Possession of an invoice is necessary but not sufficient. This is why GSTR-2B matching is the practical control, and why an unmatched credit must be reversed with interest rather than carried.

entries.title: EOQ minimises ordering plus carrying cost, not total cost
entries.body: EOQ = √(2AO/C). At the EOQ, ordering cost equals carrying cost. It ignores quantity discounts, seasonality and supplier reliability, which is why the theoretical EOQ is a starting point for negotiation, not a decision.

entries.title: The three statements are one equation
entries.body: Profit feeds retained earnings; retained earnings feeds the balance sheet; the balance sheet change feeds the cash flow. If a model does not balance, the plug is usually in working capital, tax or the debt schedule. Always build the balance check before building the statements.

entries.title: ICMAI Syllabus 2022 curriculum
entries.body: The primary source for section weights, paper names and study material. Always check the edition notified for your attempt, because amendments and study material revisions are issued periodically.

entries.title: Income-tax Department e-filing portal
entries.body: Authoritative for the current Act text, rules, forms and utilities. Use it rather than third-party summaries when a provision or a rate is in doubt.

entries.title: GST portal
entries.body: Authoritative for notifications, circulars, return formats and e-way bill rules. GST changes by notification, so the portal is the only reliable source for thresholds and rates.

entries.title: Variance analysis is a question, not a score
entries.body: A variance is only useful if it triggers an investigation or confirms control. Report the amount, the direction, the likely cause, the controllable portion and the action. An adverse variance with no action is just arithmetic.

entries.title: Ethics answers are graded on structure
entries.body: Use: issue, stakeholders, applicable principle, options, evaluation, recommendation, consequence. Name the code of ethics principles (integrity, objectivity, professional competence, confidentiality, professional behaviour) and the specific action. Application to the facts earns more than theory.

entries.title: I wrote the wrong instrument in a bank reconciliation
entries.body: Cause: treating unpresented cheques as an error. Rule: unpresented cheques and deposits in transit are timing differences, not errors; do not write them off. Only genuine errors and irrecoverable items are adjusted.

entries.title: Provision, reserve and contingent liability
entries.body: A provision is a present obligation of uncertain timing or amount recognised as a charge. A reserve is an appropriation of profit, not an obligation. A contingent liability is a possible obligation disclosed by note and not recognised. Using these three interchangeably is the most common vocabulary error in accounting interviews.

entries.title: Why discounted cash flow beats payback for decisions
entries.body: Payback measures how quickly the money returns, not whether the project creates value. It ignores everything after the payback date and treats a rupee in year 5 the same as a rupee in year 1. NPV measures value created after charging for time and risk. Use payback for liquidity context, not as the decision rule.

entries.title: Case 01 — Sundar Precision contribution analysis
entries.body: Decomposed a ₹7.1 crore EBIT decline into variable cost inflation (₹5.8 crore), volume gain (₹3.2 crore) and fixed cost growth (₹4.05 crore), and recommended price recovery plus a rejection-rate programme. Lesson: the loudest explanation in the room is rarely the largest driver.

entries.title: Company law revision spine
entries.body: Twelve anchors: incorporation (Sec 3), memorandum and articles (Secs 4-5), types of companies (Sec 2), share capital (Secs 43-55), deposits (Secs 73-76), directors (Secs 149-167), meetings (Secs 96-122), charges (Secs 77-87), dividends (Sec 123), related party transactions (Sec 188), audit (Secs 139-148), winding up (Secs 270-303). Attach one case or illustration to each anchor.
